history.period: 4th century AD (legendary foundation); renovated 1480 by Ahom king Susenpha
history.summary: The Nagsankar (Nag-Sankar) Temple is an ancient Shiva shrine at Nagsankar Mouza near Sootea, east of Tezpur and about 15 km west of Biswanath Chariali. It is traditionally said to have been built in the 4th century AD by King Narasankar (Nag Sankar) of Nagakha of the Lohitya dynasty; another legend attributes it to King Nagmatta (Arimatta), and Ahom king Susenpha (Su-sen-pha) repaired it in 1480. The temple's name was originally Navishankar, later becoming Nagshankar. It is famous for its large pond housing 500+ rare soft-shell turtles (Nilssonia gangetica and Chitra indica) and has been designated a model temple for turtle conservation. Coordinates are approximate (geocoder district-level match for Sootea; no published POI coordinates found). District note: Wikipedia lists Sonitpur, but the Biswanath district (Govt of Assam) website also lists this temple; Biswanath district was carved out of Sonitpur in 2015, so the current district may be Biswanath (verify).

name: Nag-Sankar Temple
town_description: Sootea (Sootea) is a small town in the Sonitpur/Biswanath region of Assam on the Tezpur-Biswanath Chariali road, about 15 km west of Biswanath Chariali and east of Tezpur. It is primarily known as the gateway to the ancient Nagsankar Temple nearby, set in an agricultural landscape on the north bank of the Brahmaputra. Town corrected from CSV ('Sonitpur' is the district, not a town).

travel.airport: Tezpur Airport (Salonibari), approx. 35-40 km west; taxis and buses to Sootea/Jamugurihat.
travel.railway: Tezpur Railway Station approx. 25 km west; Biswanath Chariali station approx. 15 km east.
travel.road: On the Tezpur-Biswanath Chariali road corridor (NH-15 region), about 15 km west of Biswanath Chariali near Sootea/Jamugurihat; reachable by bus, taxi and auto-rickshaw from Tezpur.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Maha Shivaratri draws the largest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not documented in the sources consulted (verify). Typically open morning to evening for daily worship; the turtle pond is a key visitor attraction.
